chapter: Big band, Chicago players, recordings and gospel
title: Cutting contests and Monday jam sessions in Chicago
summary: Chicago had sessions but not Kansas City's obsession; Monday morning jams at the Pershing Hotel bar in the 1950s trained players like Von Freeman.

story.theme_name: Coming to New York: clubs, jams, and making it
story.community_name: Making it in New York: arrival, clubs and the scene

blocks.x: But were there ever many cutting
contests around Chicago? I know there were in New York, and you were talking about them in Kansas City.
Was there very much of that in Chicago?

Well, we'd have it, but not to the extent of, like, Kansas City. They were obsessed with it. Because, I mean, if you lived in Kansas City you had to be the greatest in the world, you know. But, yeah, there were, a lot of them. They used to have these sessions here, and then over here on Monday mornings they used to have the jam sessions which would -- and that's what they really amounted to, was over there in the Pershing Hotel, there, in the bar there. They had that for years.
Yeah. When was this? This was in the '50s, the '40s?
Yeah, right. This was in the '50s and the early -- the first part of the '60s. And guys like -- this is where guys like Von Freeman and them cut their teeth.
